title: Types of Breast Lift: Crescent, Donut, Lollipop, Anchor
meta_description: The four types of breast lift are crescent, donut, lollipop and anchor. Where each scar sits, how much lift each gives, and how a surgeon chooses.
excerpt: A breast lift is named for its incision. Here is where the crescent, donut, lollipop and anchor scars sit, how much lift each gives, which go with implants and how a surgeon chooses.
quick_answer:
What are the types of breast lift?

There are four main types, named for their incisions: crescent, donut, lollipop and anchor. The Aesthetic Society matches them to minor, mild, moderate and severe sagging. More lift usually means more scar, so the anchor lifts most and scars most. Your surgeon recommends one after looking at your skin, shape and sagging.

sources.title: Breast lift procedure steps
quotes: There are three common incision patterns:
Around the areola and vertically down from the areola to the breast crease
Around the areola, vertically down from the breast crease and horizontally along the breast crease
Skin quality and elasticity as well as the amount of extra skin
Many women desire the smallest scar possible. However, your plastic surgeon will recommend the incisions which best suit your anatomy.
Listen to your surgeon and do not diminish your result by demanding an incision that will not be appropriate for you.

quotes: Implants can be placed at the same time or as a second procedure, depending on the experience of the surgeon.

sources.title: Breast lift results
quotes: The results of your breast lift surgery will be long-lasting. Over time, your breasts can continue to change due to aging and gravity.

sources.title: Breast Lift: Detailed Procedure Information
quotes: In general, the more incisions the surgeon makes, the greater the ability the surgeon has to modify the breast.

If you have a severe degree of sagging or are getting a breast reduction with your breast lift, your surgeon will likely recommend this approach. This technique produces the greatest lift, but also leaves the most scars.
If you have a moderate degree of sagging and do not want breast implants, your surgeon will likely recommend this approach. This technique produces moderate scarring.
If you have a mild degree of sagging or asymmetric areolas, your surgeon may recommend this approach.
This technique produces the least amount of scarring.
This technique is less common.

If you have minor sagging or are getting a breast lift in conjunction with breast augmentation, your surgeon may recommend this approach. You will not get the same degree of lifting with this approach as you would with other incision techniques.
In some patients, it may be possible to avoid the horizontal incision beneath the breast and the vertical incision that runs from the bottom edge of the areola to the breast crease.
However, these options all require incisions of some sort, no matter how small or well-hidden.
you will not have the same amount of lift as the other techniques, and the results are not as long-lasting.
Your nipples and areolas will remain attached to underlying mounds of tissue to preserve sensation and the ability to breastfeed.

sources.title: Breast Lift (Mastopexy): Surgery & Recovery
quotes: Crescent: This incision is a half-circle along the top half of your areola. It’s usually only used for breast augmentation in women who have little sagging.
Donut: This common incision circles your entire areola.
Vertical or lollipop lift: This incision goes in a circle around the entire areola, then vertically down from your areola to your breast crease. This is another common incision type.
It’s often used in people with more sagging or who are also having breast reduction.
The results of a breast list should last for several years.
Pregnancy and weight changes may affect the results of mastopexy.
Inability to lactate (breastfeed) in the future.

sources.title: Breast Lift
quotes: Standard Breast Lift Surgery: This procedure uses an anchor or keyhole incision, with final scars around the areola straight down and hidden in the fold of the breast. This technique creates an anchor shape and is the most common incision pattern used.
This procedure is also called a Benelli lift or periareolar lift.

sources.title: Mastopexy (Breast Lift) (Toomey AE, Cape JD, last updated December 11, 2024)
quotes: Mastopexy techniques include the crescent lift mastopexy, circumareolar mastopexy, vertical mastopexy, and wise pattern mastopexy, also called anchor pattern or inverted T.
This decision should be based on the patient's anatomy and degree of ptosis, as well as the amount of breast scarring that the patient is willing to accept.
a superior crescent of tissue at the NAC margin is excised, and the remaining skin is sutured closed to lift the NAC very slightly.
Advantages : The scar is short and hidden in the areolar border; typically, nipple sensation is unchanged.

This procedure can lead to the elongation of or misshapen areolas due to uneven tension only on the superior portion. Crescent mastopexy is only an option for very minimal lifts and scant skin excess.
A circumareolar mastopexy is recommended for patients who require less than 2 cm of lift.
This incision goes around the entire areola and can be used to reduce areolar size and improve symmetry.
This technique can cause widening of the areola due to tension, decreased projection of the breast, and potential for changes in nipple sensation.
A vertical mastopexy or lollipop incision is used when the NAC needs a greater lift length, and the skin envelope needs tightening.
this procedure can lead to an increased length of the nipple to inframammary fold distance, which can cause abnormal breast proportions.
Another disadvantage of this technique is a more apparent vertical scar in addition to the periareolar scar.
If an augmentation is performed with a vertical mastopexy, the dissection is done through this vertical incision.
The horizontal portion of the incision/scar is usually well hidden in the inframammary fold
A greater extent of scarring occurs, as well as potential healing issues at the T zone of the incisions.
Patients that have severe ptosis, wish for a large volume implant, have poor skin elasticity, or require a large amount of skin excision will typically fare better with a 2-stage procedure
Nerve injury is rare but occurs more with the wise pattern mastopexy and mastopexy with augmentation

No price per type, no statement of which incision any Alluring price covers (owner questions), and no mention of the sheet's 'modified' lift. StatPearls' 'less than 2 cm' and the 2014 review's '2 cm' are the only centimeter figures, both on how far a periareolar lift can move the nipple; no centimeter cut-offs for sagging grades. The Pontes 2021 short-scar group isn't called lollipop because its abstract says only 'short-scar'.
